description: Day-to-day use cases for AWS DevOps Agent, AWS Security Agent and AWS FinOps Agent. Delivery mode distinguishes built-in functions, configured workflows, controlled actions and team-composed procedures.

entries.title: Incident signal triage
entries.summary: Classify an incoming alert or ticket as linked to existing work, skipped by an approved rule, or eligible for a new investigation.
entries.inputs: Incident identity, correlation evidence, skip criteria and active investigations.
entries.output: Triage decision, reason and resulting investigation linkage.
entries.constraints: A triage decision is not a diagnosis. Incorrect linking or skipping requires a routing correction.
entries.example: Explain why this alert was linked, skipped or scheduled for a new investigation.

entries.title: Root-cause investigation
entries.summary: Correlate available metrics, logs, traces, code changes, deployment history and topology for a scoped production incident.
entries.inputs: Incident signal, service scope, UTC window, connected telemetry and deployment context.
entries.output: Investigation record with observations, hypotheses, root-cause versions and evidence.
entries.constraints: The output remains an investigation result to verify against current source data.
entries.example: Investigate the checkout 5xx increase for the stated service and UTC window; separate observations, hypotheses and missing data.

entries.title: Investigation steering and hypothesis review
entries.summary: Provide contrary evidence or missing context during an active investigation and obtain a revised analysis.
entries.inputs: Active investigation, operator question, new evidence or rejected hypothesis.
entries.output: Updated investigation or root-cause version that records the steering input.
entries.constraints: Steering changes analysis; it does not authorize a production action.
entries.example: The database pool is healthy. Re-evaluate the upstream dependency hypothesis and cite the current evidence.

entries.title: Mitigation plan preparation
entries.summary: Produce a reviewable mitigation candidate with target, expected effect, risks, rollback and verification steps.
entries.inputs: Reviewed incident evidence and a specific operational objective.
entries.output: Mitigation proposal suitable for operator approval or normal runbook execution.
entries.constraints: A proposal is not permission to execute. Unsupported or high-risk actions remain outside the action path.
entries.example: Propose the lowest-risk mitigation, including blast radius, rollback and recovery checks.

entries.title: Approved directed mitigation
entries.summary: Execute an eligible state-changing AWS or connected-tool operation after layered enablement and exact operator approval.
entries.availability: GA operations; directed actions require opt-in
entries.inputs: Directed-action enablement, eligible role or integration, correct tool classification and exact operation/resource approval.
entries.output: Attributed action record and independently checked resulting state.
entries.constraints: Approval is scoped to a particular operation and resource. Tool misclassification can change expected approval behavior.
entries.example: After showing the exact target and parameters, request approval for the narrowly scoped change.

entries.title: On-demand service health query
entries.summary: Answer a scoped operational question using current and historical telemetry, alarms, deployments and incident context.
entries.inputs: Service identity, reporting window and connected metrics/logs/alarms/deployment sources.
entries.output: Timestamped health answer with source scope and missing signals.
entries.constraints: A conversational health answer does not replace monitoring or prove complete signal coverage.
entries.example: Summarize checkout health for the previous 60 minutes and state every unavailable signal.

entries.title: Minute-by-minute incident status report
entries.summary: Generate a concise rolling update for an active incident from current logs, metrics and investigation state.
entries.inputs: Custom agent, selected telemetry and incident tools, explicit five- or ten-minute window and output contract.
entries.output: Delta-focused status update: changed observations, open hypotheses, owner and next check.
entries.constraints: This is a configured workflow, not a native fixed-cadence report. Schedule cadence and data window are separate.
entries.example: Every five minutes, report only what changed in the active checkout incident and name the next verification step.

entries.title: Daily or weekly service health report
entries.summary: Produce a recurring report covering service health, incidents, deployments, trends and missing data.
entries.inputs: Named services, reporting period, selected tools, reporting standard and recipients.
entries.output: Structured health report or artifact with evidence links and data-quality notes.
entries.constraints: The agent can report only from attached memory and selected tools. A schedule does not define report scope by itself.
entries.example: Generate the weekly payments health report for complete UTC days, including error, latency, incidents, deployments and data gaps.

entries.title: Deployment and change activity report
entries.summary: Summarize deployments, failed releases, rollback events and affected services over a defined period.
entries.inputs: CI/CD integration, service ownership, revision identifiers and complete reporting window.
entries.output: Deployment report with revisions, outcomes, affected services and unresolved follow-up.
entries.constraints: Requires connected pipeline tools and explicit interpretation of deployment states.
entries.example: List production deployments in the last seven complete days, including failed changes and linked incidents.

entries.title: Operational review pack
entries.summary: Assemble a weekly or monthly review combining service health, incident trends, prevention work, deployments and action owners.
entries.inputs: Review template, selected data sources, attached reporting context and named audience.
entries.output: Review agenda, evidence summary, decisions required and owned follow-up.
entries.constraints: This is a team-defined workflow. The report contract, recipients and stop owner must be configured.
entries.example: Prepare the weekly operational review pack with health, incidents, improvements, deployments, decisions and owners.

entries.title: Incident pattern identification
entries.summary: Analyze investigation history to identify recurring causes, similar incidents and systemic operational themes.
entries.inputs: Recent investigation history and managed learning context.
entries.output: Pattern summary, recurring-cause context and candidate prevention themes.
entries.constraints: Historical similarity does not establish the cause of a new incident.
entries.example: Identify recurring checkout incident patterns and cite the investigations that support each pattern.

entries.title: Prevention recommendation backlog
entries.summary: Review, prioritize and track recommendations across observability, infrastructure, governance and code optimization.
entries.inputs: Multiple incident investigations, team priorities and recommendation evaluation.
entries.output: Ranked recommendations with source incidents, expected effect and backlog state.
entries.constraints: Recommendations are not automatically implemented and may age out when not kept or implemented.
entries.example: Run a prevention evaluation and return the highest-priority recommendations with affected incidents and owners.

entries.title: Recurring root-cause recall
entries.summary: Use monitor-specific memory from previous investigations as contextual evidence in a later incident.
entries.inputs: Prior completed investigations, active monitor memory and current incident evidence.
entries.output: Retrieved historical context considered alongside current telemetry.
entries.constraints: Memory existence, retrieval and diagnostic correctness are separate observations.
entries.example: Compare this alarm with relevant prior causes, then list the current evidence that supports or contradicts each one.

entries.title: SOP consolidation into reusable skills
entries.summary: Convert an approved operational procedure into a targeted skill with applicability rules and supporting references.
entries.inputs: Reviewed SOP, target agent types, actual tool names and expected evidence.
entries.output: Version-controlled SKILL.md bundle and a matching/nonmatching selection test.
entries.constraints: Consolidation and review are team work. A skill supplies procedure; it does not grant tools or permissions.
entries.example: Create a skill from the approved checkout timeout SOP and state when it should and should not load.

entries.title: Standing operational policy
entries.summary: Apply always-on guidance such as evidence formatting, escalation or safety rules to new sessions.
entries.inputs: Reviewed global or agent-specific AGENTS.md content.
entries.output: New sessions that include the standing guidance.
entries.constraints: Instructions guide behavior but do not enforce IAM authorization. Existing sessions retain their startup content.
entries.example: Apply the evidence-output contract to new incident RCA sessions and compare with an existing session.

entries.title: Topology documentation and dependency map
entries.summary: Use discovered resources and inferred relationships to document service, repository, pipeline and dependency context.
entries.inputs: Connected accounts, discovery, Resource Explorer where applicable and relevant integrations.
entries.output: Topology view and environment summary that can support architecture documentation.
entries.constraints: Topology is a representation, not an authorization boundary or guaranteed complete inventory.
entries.example: Document the payments service containers, downstream dependencies, repositories and deployment boundaries; mark inferred relationships.

entries.title: Environment summary and topology refresh
entries.summary: Refresh learned environment understanding after integration or infrastructure changes and inspect the new version.
entries.inputs: Changed resources or integrations and managed learning capability.
entries.output: Updated environment summary, topology and versioned knowledge.
entries.constraints: A refresh request is not completion evidence. Managed learning schedules are platform-owned.
entries.example: Refresh the environment understanding after the new inventory integration and report the resulting version and changed relationships.

entries.title: Configuration audit
entries.summary: Periodically compare selected resource configurations with organizational standards and produce findings.
entries.inputs: Read-only configuration tools, approved standard, selected resource scope and report format.
entries.output: Audit findings with resource identifiers, rule and observed value.
entries.constraints: Requires explicit tools and standards. It is not a built-in universal compliance engine.
entries.example: Audit staging security-group and logging settings against the attached operations standard; do not change resources.

entries.title: Metrics and error trend analysis
entries.summary: Analyze a defined time series for trend, seasonality, error-pattern or capacity changes.
entries.inputs: Selected metric/log tools, complete time range, aggregation and comparison basis.
entries.output: Trend report with material changes, possible explanations and missing evidence.
entries.constraints: The workflow must define aggregation and avoid treating correlation as cause.
entries.example: Analyze checkout latency and error trends for the last four complete weeks and identify material changes.

entries.title: Cross-tool operational correlation
entries.summary: Combine observability, deployment, ticketing and AWS resource data to answer a bounded operational question.
entries.inputs: Selected tools from multiple providers, shared identifiers and explicit question.
entries.output: Evidence table linking signals across systems and unresolved mismatches.
entries.constraints: Tool availability and identity mapping must be explicit; similar timestamps do not prove causality.
entries.example: Correlate the error increase with deployments, alerts and tickets using service and revision identifiers.

entries.title: Release readiness review
entries.summary: Review a proposed code change, dependencies and operational risk before release.
entries.availability: Preview; feature and repository eligibility specific
entries.inputs: Candidate revision, repositories, topology and release context.
entries.output: Readiness findings, risk explanations and recommended actions.
entries.constraints: Do not apply production-operations GA status to this preview path.
entries.example: Review the retry-policy change for dependency, IAM, resilience and operational risks.

entries.title: Active release testing
entries.summary: Exercise a deployed web application or API in an authorized test environment and record observed behavior.
entries.inputs: Disposable staging target, test identities, disabled external effects and explicit allowed operations.
entries.output: Test results, reproduction detail and residual risk.
entries.constraints: Requests can create, modify or delete application data. Infrastructure write controls do not make application testing read-only.
entries.example: Test the staging checkout API with synthetic data; avoid production endpoints and external notifications.

entries.title: On-demand application penetration test
entries.summary: Run an authorized application-focused penetration test against configured non-production targets.
entries.inputs: Agent Space, verified target, written authority, test data and stop owner.
entries.output: Assessment run with findings, evidence and coverage record.
entries.constraints: Testing sends real requests and can change application state. Domain verification is not sufficient authorization.
entries.example: Run the authorized staging penetration test with the stated target, exclusions and test identities.

entries.title: Authenticated workflow assessment
entries.summary: Assess protected application routes using representative test identities and current login instructions.
entries.inputs: Credential strategy, login instructions, protected routes and representative roles.
entries.output: Findings and coverage tied to the actual authenticated identity.
entries.constraints: Credential retrieval and application authentication are separate steps.
entries.example: Assess the invoice workflow as the test customer role and record the identity and routes reached.

entries.title: Private application assessment
entries.summary: Assess an authorized application reachable only through configured VPC connectivity.
entries.inputs: Target rules, VPC route, DNS, security groups and application credentials.
entries.output: Reachability record and assessment findings for the private target.
entries.constraints: Private reachability does not broaden the authorized target list or credential scope.
entries.example: Assess the private staging endpoint and confirm that the production callback remains out of scope.

entries.title: Recurring penetration test
entries.summary: Run the same saved penetration-test configuration on a recurring schedule to obtain separate assessment runs.
entries.inputs: Stable saved configuration, current test credentials, authorized target and schedule.
entries.output: Separate scheduled run records and findings.
entries.constraints: Each run reflects the then-current target and credentials; a schedule does not guarantee successful authentication.
entries.example: Schedule the staging penetration test weekly and retain each run as a separate evidence record.

entries.title: Login procedure reuse
entries.summary: Reuse a previously successful authentication navigation workflow in later test sessions and runs.
entries.inputs: At least one successful login, saved penetration-test configuration and Login Optimization enabled.
entries.output: Reused login skill and observed authenticated identity.
entries.constraints: The learned procedure concerns login navigation, not general vulnerability learning.
entries.example: Compare first-run and later login behavior, then verify the actual application role.

entries.title: Finding review and prioritization
entries.summary: Review impact, confidence, reproduction steps, affected data and business context before disposition.
entries.inputs: Completed assessment findings and application-owner context.
entries.output: Prioritized finding with owner, disposition and remediation plan.
entries.constraints: Finding count or severity alone is not an adequate risk decision.
entries.example: Prioritize the findings using impact, confidence, affected role and reproduction evidence.

entries.title: Jira remediation tracking
entries.summary: Create a Jira issue for an accepted finding and keep remediation and revalidation updates linked.
entries.inputs: Finding, connected Jira project and approved disclosure scope.
entries.output: Jira issue linked to the finding, with later revalidation comments when supported.
entries.constraints: Sensitive assessment details should not be published to an inappropriate project or audience.
entries.example: Create a Jira issue for this accepted finding with the evidence, affected revision and acceptance test.

entries.title: Proposed code remediation
entries.summary: Generate a repository change proposal for an accepted finding and send it through normal engineering review.
entries.inputs: Accepted finding, repository access and remediation configuration.
entries.output: Patch or pull request linked to the finding.
entries.constraints: A proposed patch is not a reviewed, deployed or verified repair.
entries.example: Prepare a remediation change for the authorization finding and include tests; do not merge automatically.

entries.title: Finding revalidation
entries.summary: Retest selected existing findings after the repair is deployed to the original authorized target.
entries.inputs: Completed original finding, deployed repair and current authentication configuration.
entries.output: Separate revalidation job linked to the original finding with Active or Resolved result.
entries.constraints: Revalidation does not rediscover unrelated vulnerabilities or establish whole-application security.
entries.example: Revalidate the selected finding against the deployed revision and record the actual test identity.

entries.title: Repository code review
entries.summary: Analyze a configured repository or supported source package for vulnerabilities and enabled security requirements.
entries.inputs: Connected repository or S3 source, review mode and applicable requirement packs.
entries.output: Code findings with evidence, location and possible remediation.
entries.constraints: Provider, source and availability limits apply. Completed review is not complete application coverage.
entries.example: Review the repository for vulnerability findings and the enabled authorization requirements.

entries.title: Change-focused code review
entries.summary: Assess a pull request, merge request or differential source so findings are tied to a specific change.
entries.inputs: Supported change event or differential source, repository context and criteria.
entries.output: Revision-specific findings and optional remediation path.
entries.constraints: Subsequent changes may require a new review; support differs by provider and trigger path.
entries.example: Review this change for security findings and enabled requirements; identify the exact revision.

entries.title: Security requirement evaluation
entries.summary: Evaluate design or code evidence against reviewed applicability and compliance criteria.
entries.inputs: Enabled requirement pack and eligible assessment configured for requirement evaluation.
entries.output: Requirement-level compliant, violating or inapplicable result.
entries.constraints: A framework or generated pack is not a compliance certification.
entries.example: Evaluate the ownership-check requirement and show why it is applicable, compliant or violated.

entries.title: Security requirement consolidation
entries.summary: Generate or consolidate a requirement pack from authoritative policy documents and review the replacement before enablement.
entries.inputs: Governed policy sources, existing pack and reviewer.
entries.output: Reviewed replacement requirement pack and external change record.
entries.constraints: Regeneration replaces existing requirements, including manual entries. Keep the authoritative source outside the generated pack.
entries.example: Regenerate the pack from the approved policy documents and identify which existing requirements would be replaced.

entries.title: Design review
entries.summary: Assess a design document against security requirements before implementation or release.
entries.inputs: Current design material, application context and enabled requirement packs.
entries.output: Design findings and reviewed assumptions.
entries.constraints: Design review uses a different one-off lifecycle from reusable run configurations.
entries.example: Review the new payment design against the enabled security requirements and list unsupported assumptions.

entries.title: Threat modeling
entries.summary: Build and review a threat model from connected architecture and scope material.
entries.inputs: Architecture documents, code/context sources and explicit system boundary.
entries.output: Assets, trust boundaries, flows, threats and model findings.
entries.constraints: Inferred system context requires review; the model is not a complete guarantee of threat coverage.
entries.example: Create a threat model for the checkout service and mark inferred flows that require owner confirmation.

entries.title: CI/CD assessment integration
entries.summary: Start a previously configured assessment from a delivery workflow and record the server-side job result.
entries.inputs: Saved assessment configuration, pipeline credentials and explicit pass/fail policy.
entries.output: Assessment job and auditable delivery decision.
entries.constraints: The pipeline runner is not the assessment engine. Missing or inconclusive evidence needs an explicit gate policy.
entries.example: Start the configured staging assessment from the release pipeline and fail safely on missing evidence.

entries.title: Natural-language cost inquiry
entries.summary: Ask a bounded cost question in plain language using authorized cost and usage data.
entries.inputs: Dates, cost metric, currency, account scope and requested dimension.
entries.output: Answer with figures, filters and source context.
entries.constraints: A fluent answer is not a substitute for a reproducible source query.
entries.example: Show production storage cost for the last complete week by account and Region; state the metric and filters.

entries.title: Cost variance decomposition
entries.summary: Compare complete periods and quantify the service, usage or rate components contributing to the change.
entries.inputs: Comparable windows, same cost basis, grouping dimensions and source permissions.
entries.output: Reconciled delta and ranked contributors.
entries.constraints: Contribution arithmetic does not by itself establish the operational cause.
entries.example: Compare the last two complete weeks and decompose the cost delta into usage and rate changes.

entries.title: Cost breakdown by ownership dimension
entries.summary: Group cost by account, service, Region, tag or organization-specific owner mapping.
entries.inputs: Authorized cost data, grouping dimension and optional context file mapping.
entries.output: Dimensioned totals and unmapped items.
entries.constraints: Owner mappings require maintained context; tags and account metadata may be incomplete.
entries.example: Break down this cost by service owner and list every unmapped account or tag.

entries.title: Forecast and commitment coverage review
entries.summary: Review forecasts or commitment coverage as separate analytical questions from historical cost.
entries.inputs: Forecast horizon, commitment scope and relevant upstream source.
entries.output: Forecast or coverage summary with assumptions.
entries.constraints: Forecast and recommendation values are not observed spend and should not be combined without qualification.
entries.example: Summarize the next-month forecast and current commitment coverage; separate observed and projected values.

entries.title: Daily, weekly or monthly cost report
entries.summary: Generate a recurring cost report with a fixed basis, sections, audience and downloadable artifact.
entries.inputs: Report contract, schedule, source scope, context and recipients.
entries.output: HTML, PDF or editable presentation artifact.
entries.constraints: Schedule, source window and audience are separate settings. Report values still require reconciliation.
entries.example: Create a weekly cost report with service totals, anomalies, recommendations, owners and unresolved gaps.

entries.title: FinOps operational review pack
entries.summary: Assemble a cross-functional review of cost movement, anomalies, recommendations, decisions and measured outcomes.
entries.inputs: Recurring report, owner mappings, recommendation status and review template.
entries.output: Review agenda, decision log and owner/action table.
entries.constraints: The review process and acceptance criteria are team-defined, not a separate native feature.
entries.example: Prepare the monthly FinOps review pack with decisions required, owners and prior action outcomes.

entries.title: On-demand cost anomaly investigation
entries.summary: Investigate a detected cost anomaly and rank root causes by cost impact.
entries.inputs: Cost Anomaly Detection record, Cost Explorer access and optional CloudTrail permission.
entries.output: Anomaly explanation with affected services, usage/rate analysis and correlated changes.
entries.constraints: CloudTrail events are correlated activity, not automatic proof of cause.
entries.example: Investigate the MemoryDB anomaly and separate usage, rate and correlated change evidence.

entries.title: Event-triggered anomaly response
entries.summary: Automatically create a task when a matching cost anomaly event occurs and publish or retain the result.
entries.inputs: Anomaly monitor, event-rule permission, automation condition and optional destination.
entries.output: Task history, investigation result and delivery status.
entries.constraints: The documented event source is Cost Anomaly Detection. Removing the automation stops future tasks, not existing records.
entries.example: When a production anomaly exceeds the threshold, investigate it and post the result to the approved channel.

entries.title: Optimization recommendation triage
entries.summary: Review upstream optimization recommendations against service constraints and overlapping estimates.
entries.inputs: Cost Optimization Hub or Compute Optimizer recommendation, workload evidence and owner constraints.
entries.output: Prioritized candidate, rejected/deferred reason and accepted next step.
entries.constraints: The agent contextualizes upstream recommendations; it does not independently calculate or authorize the change.
entries.example: Review the storage recommendations, identify overlapping savings and list the reliability constraints.

entries.title: Post-change savings measurement
entries.summary: Measure an independently authorized change using comparable cost and service-health windows.
entries.inputs: Implemented change record, comparable periods and service indicators.
entries.output: Measured outcome with attribution limits.
entries.constraints: A lower bill does not prove the change caused the decrease; traffic, prices and allocation may differ.
entries.example: Compare the post-change period with a matched baseline and state what cannot be attributed to the change.

entries.title: Cost ownership and allocation context
entries.summary: Provide account-to-team mappings, reporting basis and organizational conventions through maintained reference files.
entries.inputs: Supported context file with non-sensitive ownership and allocation data.
entries.output: Context available to relevant tasks and conversations.
entries.constraints: Files are visible to agent users, cannot be conversationally rewritten and have file/total size limits.
entries.example: Use the approved account-owner mapping and list every cost item that lacks an owner.

entries.title: Persistent reporting preferences
entries.summary: Retain non-sensitive preferences, corrections and owner details across conversations.
entries.inputs: Explicit remember, update or forget request.
entries.output: Agent-instance memory applied in later sessions.
entries.constraints: Memory is distinct from reference files and should be tested independently.
entries.example: Remember that executive reports use amortized cost and update the preference when the policy changes.

entries.title: Scheduled recurring task
entries.summary: Create a schedule that produces a new queued task at each interval.
entries.inputs: Prompt, schedule, tools/data permissions and output expectations.
entries.output: Automation record and separate task history.
entries.constraints: Deleting an automation stops future starts but does not delete existing tasks or messages.
entries.example: Run the weekly optimization review every Monday at the stated UTC time.

entries.title: Jira follow-up creation
entries.summary: Create an issue or comment that turns a reviewed cost analysis into owned follow-up.
entries.inputs: Connected Jira project, reviewed content and owner.
entries.output: Jira issue/comment and task history.
entries.constraints: Interactive and on-demand Jira actions require approval; automation actions are pre-authorized at setup.
entries.example: Create a Jira issue for the accepted storage optimization with evidence, owner and acceptance criteria.

entries.title: Slack publication
entries.summary: Post a reviewed cost or anomaly summary to a configured Slack channel.
entries.inputs: Registered workspace, agent connection, channel and reviewed message scope.
entries.output: Slack post and delivery result.
entries.constraints: Slack posting has no approval prompt, including interactive use; channel membership and sensitive content must be reviewed.
entries.example: Post the approved anomaly summary to the FinOps incident channel.

entries.title: Downloadable report artifact
entries.summary: Generate, revise and retain a report artifact for review or distribution.
entries.inputs: Source query, report instructions and desired format.
entries.output: HTML, PDF or editable presentation artifact.
entries.constraints: Formatting quality does not establish numerical or causal accuracy; external copies have their own lifecycle.
entries.example: Generate an editable monthly cost report and include the query basis for every chart.
